name: Sri Kaleshwara Mukteshwara Swamy Devasthanam
address: Executive Officer, Sri Kaleshwara Mukteshwara Swamy Devasthanam, Kaleshwaram Village, Mahadevpur Mandal, Jayashankar Bhupalpally District, Telangana - 505504
river: Dakshina Triveni Sangamam (River Godavari, River Pranahita, and subterranean River Saraswati)
main_deity: Lord Kaleshwara (representing Lord Yama / Time) & Lord Mukteshwara (representing Lord Shiva / Liberation) on a single pedestal (Panavattam)
description: Abode of Lord Kaleshwara & Lord Mukteshwara – at Kaleshwaram village is one of the most ancient, revered, and architecturally unique Shaivite shrines in South India. The presiding deity is unique because two Shiva Lingas—Lord Kaleshwara and Lord Mukteshwara—are enshrined together on a single pedestal (Panavattam). Another divine wonder is the presence of two distinct nostrils (Nasarandhras) on the Mukteshwara Linga. Water poured during Abhishekam into these openings flows through subterranean channels and drains directly into the holy Triveni Sangam river bed. Devotees must first worship Lord Kaleshwara before proceeding to Lord Mukteshwara.
history:
Skanda Purana mentions that Lord Yama Dharma Raja performed severe penance at this spot after discovering that devotees worshipping Lord Shiva here were directly attaining salvation, leaving Yama's realm (Yama Loka) empty. Pleased with his penance, Lord Shiva granted Yama a spot alongside Him on the same pedestal and ordained that Yama (Kaleshwara) be worshipped first.

Kaleshwaram is also revered as one of the cornerstone shrines of Telugu heritage under the 'Trilinga Desam' connection, bounded by three famous shrines: Srisailam (Andhra Pradesh), Draksharamam (Andhra Pradesh), and Kaleshwaram (Telangana).
mythology: Lord Shiva granted Yama a spot alongside Him on the same pedestal. Devotees worship Lord Yama first to destroy fear of death and grant ultimate liberation (Moksha). Worshipping the twin Lingas together is a unique spiritual custom.

sub_temples.name: Sri Subhananda Devi Temple
sub_temples.significance: Dedicated to Goddess Parvati, divine consort of Mukteshwara Swamy.

highlights.name: Intricate stone pillars and carvings
highlights.description: Intricate stone pillars, sanctum carvings, and historic outer walls built during the 10th to 12th centuries AD.
